data.title: DefiLlama data shows 71% of blockchains generated zero fees in 24 hours
data.description:
Most blockchains are open for business. Very few have customers.

On October 3, 2026, DefiLlama's chain fees dashboard tracked 558 blockchains. Of those, 399 generated zero fees over the previous 24 hours, roughly 71% of the entire field.

The numbers get starker one level up. According to the same DefiLlama data, 443 of the 558 tracked chains collected less than $10 in fees during that 24-hour window.

At the other end of the table, only seven blockchains cleared $100,000 in fees over the same period. The leaderboard looked like this:

Solana: $1.09 millionTron: $922,900BSC (Binance Smart Chain): $793,900Ethereum: $435,000Bitcoin: $325,600Base: $114,800Robinhood Chain: $100,900

Solana was the only network to break the $1 million mark. Tron and BSC followed close enough that the top three formed their own tier.

Ethereum and Bitcoin, the two largest names in crypto by reputation, landed in fourth and fifth. Fees measure what users paid to transact, not how important a network is, so the ranking reflects spending patterns on that day rather than a verdict on overall significance.

Base, the Ethereum layer-2 network, slipped in at sixth. Robinhood Chain barely cleared the bar in seventh, sitting just $900 above the $100,000 threshold.

This snapshot was not an outlier. DefiLlama's data showed similar concentration patterns earlier in 2026, with a small group of leading networks capturing the bulk of fee activity.

Canton Network, for instance, occasionally topped revenue charts earlier in the year, a reminder that the leaderboard is competitive even if the long tail is not.

DefiLlama updates its fees by chain rankings in real time, and the early October readings again confirmed the same basic shape. A handful of networks pull in meaningful fees, and the overwhelming majority barely register.

For investors, the data offers a useful filter. Fee generation is one of the more concrete signals in crypto, because it reflects people paying real money to do something on a network rather than simply holding a token and hoping.

By that measure, Solana, Tron and BSC showed the strongest user engagement on October 3. A chain with zero fees, meanwhile, offers little evidence that anyone is using it, whatever its marketing or token valuation might suggest.

Low fees can also be a design choice. Some networks deliberately keep transaction costs minimal, which means a modest fee total does not automatically signal an empty chain, though a total of exactly zero is harder to explain away.

Robinhood Chain's presence among the seven chains above $100,000 shows that the top tier is not completely locked, and that a well-distributed newcomer can still break in.

For anyone sizing up a new network, a simple question now carries real weight: is anyone paying to use it? On October 3, for 399 chains, the answer was no.

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Target, Moderna and PepsiCo among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the green on Friday, after the week saw latest payroll data and earnings reports from Micron and Accenture.

Nasdaq rose marginally for the week, led by Lumentum Holdings (), which advanced over 15%. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

HSBC says Target’s turnaround ‘gaining momentum’

HSBC upgraded Target to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $190 from $125, saying the company’s turnaround is "gaining momentum" and has further room to run.

Analyst Joe Thomas said second-quarter sales performance was "encouraging" and suggested the store base was not being “unduly cannibalised.”  Thomas added improvements in Beauty, Food and Beverage, Hardlines, and Household Essentials were beginning to resonate, although Apparel and Home still require further work.

HSBC raised its FY27 EPS estimate to $10.61 from $8.26 and said forecasts “look conservative.”

Moderna downgraded on ‘unjustifiable’ valuation

Citi downgraded Moderna to Sell from Neutral, citing an "unjustifiable" valuation following a late-stage trial win for its personalized cancer shot, intismeran autogene, developed with Merck .

Analyst Geoff Meacham noted that since the Phase 3 win in melanoma last August, the Massachusetts-based biotech has rallied more than 222% compared with a 2% decline in its peers as represented by the State Street SPDR S&P Biotech ETF .

“While intismeran could become a market-leading therapy in melanoma, we believe the re-rating now reflects successful expansion in many tumor types and unrealistic implied sales,” Meacham wrote, lowering his PT to $60 from $80 per share.

Deutsche Bank turns bearish on PepsiCo

Deutsche Bank downgraded PepsiCo to Hold from Buy on the view that a turnaround scenario is now complicated.

Analyst Steve Powers acknowledged the low valuation on PepsiCo but noted the firm now has less certainty in the company's strategic direction in North America and less conviction in its ability to deliver a durable recovery in the PepsiCo Foods North America segment.

Occidental Petroleum raised to Buy on strong debt reduction

Goldman Sachs upgraded Occidental Petroleum  to Buy from Neutral with a $69 price target, bumped up from $63, citing the company's differentiated advanced recovery approach, strong outlook for debt reduction and dividend growth potential, targeted $4B cash flow improvement by 2030, and an attractive risk/reward skew given the current discounted valuation.

Goldman's Neil Mehta said he has seen strong YTD share price performance from the bank's oil E&P coverage given an elevated oil pricing environment, with Occidental shares trading in line with the broader coverage despite "structural improvements that OXY has driven across its business through an incremental focus on capital efficiency and deleveraging" under new CEO Richard Jackson.

Mehta double-downgraded Tourmaline Oil to Sell from Buy with a C$49 price target, cut from C$59, citing a challenging Western Canadian natural gas macro environment in the near-term.

Wells Fargo upgraded Consolidated Edison to Overweight from Equal Weight with a $118 price target, raised from $108, viewing the stock as a "defensive diversification away from the broader AI trade."

Wells Fargo upgraded BP to Overweight from Equal Weight with a $57 price target, raised from $48, while downgrading ExxonMobil to Equal Weight from Overweight with an unchanged $182 PT, saying relative valuations are "converging in BP's favor," helped by faster debt reduction and resource development.

Nvidia was in focus as Morgan Stanley reinstated the Jensen Huang-led tech giant as its top pick in the semiconductor space.

“Nvidia remains very early in the ramp of a new product cycle, powered shell constraints play into Nvidia’s strengths, and recent agentic enthusiasm can accelerate Vera adoption,” Morgan Stanley analysts, led by Joseph Moore, wrote.

data.title: Bank of Baroda Q2 update: Global business rises 17.5% YoY to ₹32.64 lakh crore
data.description:
Bank of Baroda has reported year-on-year growth across its key business segments for the quarter ended September 2026, with both deposits and advances registering double-digit growth.

It reported a 17.45% year-on-year growth in its global business to ₹32.64 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026, according to the bank’s Q2 business update.

Global advances grew 18.27% YoY to ₹15.12 lakh crore, while global deposits increased 16.75% to ₹17.51 lakh crore during the same period.

In the domestic business, total deposits rose 17.01% YoY to ₹14.88 lakh crore as of September 30. Domestic advances grew 13.5% to ₹11.88 lakh crore.

Earlier in a separate development, on August 14, Bank informed that it has concluded the issuance of senior unsecured fixed-rate notes amounting to $700 million under its medium-term note (MTN) programme, according to an exchange filing.

The issuance comprises $400 million of notes with a three-year maturity and a coupon of 5.114% per annum, and $300 million of notes with a five-year maturity and a coupon of 5.318% per annum. The coupons are payable semi-annually.

The bonds will be issued through Bank of Baroda’s IFSC Banking Unit on August 20, 2026. The notes will be listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange, India INX and NSE-IX Exchange in GIFT City.

In another development, on Oct 1, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) has formally appointed Bank of Baroda as a sponsor of a pension fund, marking the entry of the public sector lender into the pension fund business.

Bank of Baroda received the Certificate of Appointment as Sponsor of the Pension Fund under Section 27 of the PFRDA Act, 2013, on October 1, during the NPS Divas 2026 event. The bank becomes the second public sector bank to enter the pension fund business, according to the lender.

Bank of Baroda shares closed at ₹232 on October 1, up 0.63% in the session at NSE.

data.title: Five Things I Learned in Hiring a Financial Adviser — WSJ
data.description:
By Brian Hershberg

For 25 years, I managed my family's finances myself. Then I had one of those milestone birthdays earlier this year that makes you think about life, death and, hopefully, retirement.

So I finally decided to hire a financial adviser to help.

It wasn't because I suddenly decided I couldn't manage our investments and day-to-day finances. It was because I began asking questions that I wasn't sure I could answer. What would happen if I suddenly lost my job? Have we saved enough for retirement? And if I die tomorrow, would my wife know what we owned, where everything was and what to do next?

I also worried that after several strong years for U.S. stocks, our portfolio had become too concentrated and exposed to a crash or correction. I hadn't rebalanced in years and I wanted to reduce some of that risk, diversify our holdings and start preparing for some worst-case scenarios.

My first mission was to find an adviser. As a Wall Street Journal features editor-and involved in many articles on wealth management-I knew what I wanted: a fee-only adviser who would act as a fiduciary. This would ensure that any advice would be free from conflicts of interest by commission-driven brokers or advisers. I searched the National Association of Personal Financial Advisors website and contacted several fee-only firms in my area.

I figured I also knew what to expect. But the process of interviewing advisers and eventually hiring one taught me things about financial advice that I hadn't appreciated from years of writing and editing stories about it. It also taught me a few things about myself as an investor and saver.

Here are five lessons I learned from the hiring and onboarding process.

1. The fit goes both ways

The first adviser I contacted got back to me the day before my 50th birthday, and asked about our finances. After hearing the numbers, the adviser told me I had done well.

Then came the bad news: The firm typically didn't work with clients below a certain asset level, and I wasn't even close to it.

It was a sobering rejection, and made me realize that finding an adviser isn't like hiring a contractor who actively bids for your business. Many advisory firms have a particular kind of client they serve-be it "high net worth" or company founders or some other niche.

So I kept looking and found two other advisory firms that seemed promising. The first one was close to my home, but made me nervous: While the firm accepted clients regardless of account size, it was run by a lone adviser who was relatively new to the industry. The second firm, however, had several advisers on staff, a track record of nearly 30 years and, most crucially, a willingness to work with a relatively small client.

After an initial meeting where I summarized our financial situation and heard the firm's investing and planning philosophy-a systematic approach focused on growth using primarily passively managed index mutual funds-I was ready to sign on.

But even though I managed our household finances, I was told I first had to bring my wife into the process to share her questions and perspectives on such matters as risk tolerance and retirement. That made sense. After all, how can an adviser make a holistic plan if we aren't all on the same page about our goals, our concerns or our relationship with money?

2. My finances were messier than I thought

I thought I had a pretty good handle on our finances. Then the adviser's onboarding checklist arrived.

Investment accounts were the easy part. To plan holistically for our household circumstances, the adviser wanted insurance policies, employee-benefits material, estate documents, tax information and other records that I hadn't looked at in years or knew where to find.

My filing system, such as it is, was a bit haphazard. But the exercise also had a benefit: It forced me to see the whole picture, and exposed the gaps in my system, such as a heavy tilt toward the tax-deferred savings in a 401(k) versus the posttax savings in a Roth IRA. Better to find out now rather than years from now when I'm set to retire.

3. Fee-only doesn't mean inexpensive

I knew I wanted a fee-only fiduciary adviser because I didn't want conflicted, commission-driven advice. What I hadn't fully comprehended is how much an ongoing financial advisory relationship would cost.

The firm that we hired charges an annual fee ranging from 0.5% to 1.25% of assets under management, assessed quarterly based on the market value of assets on the last business day of the previous quarter. It's a fairly typical fee arrangement for fiduciary advisers, with the percentage fee falling as your assets under management rise. Right now we are on the high end of the fee scale because most of our assets are in company-sponsored 401(k)s and so remain outside the adviser's purview.

But at some point the annual fee would rise if we choose to transfer those 401(k) savings to an individual retirement account and bring them under the advisory umbrella. The fee then will fall as a percentage of assets but the dollar amount will likely rise substantially. Thankfully that's a decision for another day.

Ultimately, for our household, we decided the cost was worth the peace of mind even if it was a bit hard to swallow. Besides portfolio management, we're paying for retirement planning-both the accumulation and decumulation phases-tax and insurance guidance, estate planning and a sounding board for decisions I had long made alone and with little regard for long-term consequences.

4. Risk is in the eye of the beholder

I went into the process primarily worried about our allocation to U.S. stocks, which far exceeded recommended norms. One of the adviser's first recommendations was to rebalance our savings across accounts and bring in greater diversity.

That brings me to one of the more surprising lessons so far: how I perceive risk. I was looking at it purely through the lens of exposure-our portfolio was overly concentrated in large-cap, domestic stocks that have surged over the past several years-and so I needed to reduce risk.

I might have done that by adding a value-stock fund, some bonds, maybe an international fund or an alternative asset class like real estate as a means of derisking and diversifying. But one of the advantages of hiring an adviser is getting a different perspective from someone who has an inside view of our holdings. And he saw our portfolio risk in a different way.

For example, I had always considered growth stocks to be riskier than value stocks as their valuations are typically higher and prices more volatile. But portfolio risk isn't a zero-sum game. Concentrating too heavily in value stocks, my adviser said, creates a risk that a portfolio won't secure the returns needed to fund a potentially long retirement.

The lesson wasn't about which class of stocks is safer, but rather that diversification means not only bulwarking your portfolio against downturns but also enhancing your chances of long-term success. Without taking an appropriate amount of risk, we'd be leaving ourselves vulnerable to falling short or having to scale back in retirement.

5. Letting go is hard

For half my life I made nearly every long-term financial decision for our household, from our 401(k) contribution rates to college financing for our son. Then I hired someone to essentially tell me that some of those decisions were wrong, or at least not in our long-term interest, and what changes to make.

I knew I wanted to rebalance our holdings across accounts and reduce the overall risk, but selling investments that had performed well was tougher than I expected. I hadn't realized how emotionally attached I had become to inanimate holdings or to my own sense of financial savvy. I still find myself at times checking prices of since-sold holdings-like a fantasy-football manager checking on what my inactive players are doing-but I am learning to take solace in the comfort of a better-balanced and more-comprehensive financial plan.

In the months since we began working with our financial adviser, I've mostly adhered to the plan and taken the prescribed actions. I'm not going to blindly follow the adviser; after all, his judgment could be flawed and he has biases just like I have mine. But even if I don't have this adviser forever, the lessons I've learned in working with him have been well worth the time and the money.

data.title: Safe: Shielded transactions with Bermuda enter beta early access - 03 Oct 2026
data.description:
Safe has opened beta early access to shielded transactions with Bermuda for professional teams. Bermuda is a compliant privacy solution funded by Gnosis. A Privacy Design Partner Program is also opening to test the transactions against real workflows.

data.title: Srirup Sircar Takes New HR Role At Cipla
data.description:
Srirup sircar moves to a wider india business mandate after more than 11 years across cipla’s hr function

Cipla has appointed Srirup Sircar as Senior Director and HR Head - Talent Acquisition, Employee Relations and HR Operations for its One India Business. Sircar takes on the expanded role in October 2026 after leading HR for the company’s Respiratory Cluster for more than five years.

New India Business Role

Sircar will oversee talent acquisition, employee relations and HR operations as part of his new mandate. The move expands his responsibilities from a business-cluster role to a broader India Business HR portfolio.

He has spent more than 11 years at Cipla, working across HR leadership and business partnering roles. His experience at the pharmaceutical company includes strategic people initiatives, HR business partnering and leadership responsibilities for the Respiratory Cluster.

Leadership Across Cipla

Sircar joined Cipla in January 2015 as Associate Director HR for the India Business, a position he held until June 2020.

He was appointed Director, Human Resources for the Respiratory Cluster in July 2020 and moved to Senior Director and HR Head for the cluster in January 2023. He held the latter position until September 2026.

During his tenure with the Respiratory Cluster, Sircar was responsible for the people agenda supporting the business. His latest appointment brings talent acquisition, employee relations and HR operations under his broader remit.

Earlier Abbott Experience

Before joining Cipla, Sircar spent more than 12 years at Abbott, where he worked as Chief Manager HR from December 2002 to January 2015.

His responsibilities at Abbott covered sales, training and HR within the pharmaceutical sector. He also worked as an HR Business Partner for assigned business units and was involved in strategic people initiatives.

His profile states that he handled a team of about 1,300 field employees across eight divisions during his Abbott tenure.

Two Decades In Pharma HR

Sircar has more than two decades of experience in human resources, primarily across the pharmaceutical sector. His career spans HR business partnering, talent acquisition, employee relations, training and people management.

He holds a PGDHR in Human Resources from the Institute of Management Technology, Ghaziabad, and a Bachelor of Science in Econometrics and Quantitative Economics from Calcutta University, Kolkata.

The appointment moves Sircar from leading HR for a specific business cluster to a wider mandate covering key HR functions across Cipla’s One India Business.

data.title: Rohit Panda Takes Charge As Head Of HR, India At Vanguard
data.description:
Rohit panda moves into the india hr leadership role as vanguard expands its presence in hyderabad

Vanguard has appointed Rohit Panda as Head of HR, India, based in Hyderabad. Panda takes on the role in October 2026 after more than two years as HR Director and Senior Business Partner for Vanguard’s Technology Division, where he also supported the HR strategy and setup for the company’s India operations.

New India HR Role

In his new position, Panda will lead the HR function for Vanguard’s India operations. His appointment comes as the global investment management company continues to establish its presence in Hyderabad.

Panda has been involved in Vanguard’s India expansion, including HR strategy and setup for the Hyderabad office. His previous responsibilities also covered HR support for outsourcing and insourcing, divestitures and change initiatives.

Experience Across HR Functions

Panda brings experience across HR business partnering, consulting, talent acquisition, people transition and change management.

Before joining Vanguard, he spent more than 14 years at Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), where he held multiple HR and consulting roles across India and North America.

From April 2017 to August 2024, Panda served as HR Director, Business Consulting, focusing on M&A, Global Capability Centre (GCC) strategy and business deals for TCS North America. His responsibilities included HR due diligence, workforce transition, integration, operating model design and people-related aspects of business transactions.

Focus On Business Transitions

Earlier at TCS, Panda worked as HR Manager, People Transition for India and North America. He supported people transition and business consulting activities across India, the US and Canada.

He also served as Programme Manager and HR Specialist for Global Talent Acquisition, working on talent management, competency development, internal rotations, succession planning, HR processes and analytics.

Panda began his TCS career as Talent Acquisition Lead for the Bengaluru and Kochi regions, where he worked on recruitment strategy and delivery for business leadership.

Broader HR Leadership

Across his career, Panda has worked on HR aspects of M&A, GCC and greenfield setups, Build-Operate-Transfer models and digital transformation programmes.

His professional experience also includes advising organisations on workforce transition, target operating models, employee integration and people processes. He holds an MBA in Human Resources from Alliance University and a certification in Human Resources Management and Services from Columbia Business School.

Panda’s move into the India HR leadership role brings his experience in business partnering, workforce transitions and large-scale organisational change to Vanguard’s growing India operations.

data.title: Navin Kumar Takes Over As Factory Head HR At Nestlé India’s Pantnagar Unit
data.description:
Navin kumar moves to pantnagar after serving as factory head hr at nestlé india’s tahliwal factory

Nestlé India has appointed Navin Kumar as Factory Head HR at its Pantnagar factory in Uttarakhand. Kumar takes charge of the role in October 2026 after serving as Factory Head HR at the company’s Tahliwal factory since April 2025. He brings more than 18 years of HR experience across manufacturing and FMCG.

Moves To Pantnagar

Kumar will lead HR responsibilities at Nestlé India’s Pantnagar factory, one of the company’s large manufacturing locations in India. His appointment marks a continuation of his HR leadership career within Nestlé, following his 18-month stint at the Tahliwal factory.

During his tenure at Tahliwal, Kumar worked on employee relations and union consultation, while also driving digital initiatives. His experience at Nestlé followed a long career in the core manufacturing sector.

Long Tata Steel Tenure

Before joining Nestlé, Kumar spent nearly 16 years at Tata Steel in a series of HR roles across its operations.

His most recent position there was Head HRBP for the Bearings Division, based in Kharagpur. Earlier, he served as Head HRBP for Shared Services TSJ in Jamshedpur and held HR leadership roles covering iron making, the CWR cell and the Noamundi OMQ Division.

Kumar also held senior HRM positions covering corporate functions, shared services and employee amenities. Earlier in his Tata Steel career, he worked as Manager HR/IR across the Jharia and OMQ divisions.

Early Career In Manufacturing

Kumar began his professional career at ACC, where he worked as Assistant Manager-HR & EW from June 2008 to June 2009.

His career has therefore covered HR roles across cement, mining, metals and FMCG, giving him experience across different manufacturing environments and employee groups.

Focus On People Practices

Kumar’s professional experience includes employee relations, HR business partnering, talent management and workplace diversity and inclusion. His profile also highlights an interest in talent development and building more diverse workplaces.

He holds a PGDPM&IR in Personnel Management from the Xavier Institute of Social Service, where he graduated with First Class with Distinction.

Kumar’s move to Pantnagar adds another manufacturing HR leadership role to his career as he takes on responsibilities at Nestlé India’s Uttarakhand facility.

data.title: "Winning Asian Games paves way for Olympics": Former Indian cricketer Madan Lal hails India's win over Pakistan
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- Former cricketer and member of India's 1983 ODI World Cup-winning team, Madan Lal, hailed the Indian men's Asian Games 2026 gold medal triumph over Pakistan as a significant achievement for Indian cricket.

He highlighted the importance of cricket's inclusion in the Olympics, saying the global platform would further enhance the team's profile and provide greater exposure.

Madan Lal also praised the squad's experience and urged the players to maintain their current approach and continue performing at the highest level.

"Cricket was included for the first time, and our team is certainly stronger than Pakistan's. It seemed likely we would win, though in T20 cricket, you never know who might come out on top. But it was a good match...Winning the Asian Games paves the way for Olympic participation, which is a massive achievement in itself, given the magnitude of the Olympics.They should just keep playing the way they are currently playing. They possess a great deal of experience," Madan Lal told ANI in New Delhi on Saturday.

Following the women's team's triumph, India's men also defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the gold medal clash at the ongoing Asian Games on Saturday, with stellar performances from Abhishek Sharma, Tilak Varma and Axar Patel powering the team to victory.

Chasing a massive target of 212, Pakistan's Hasan Nawaz stood out as a lone warrior, smashing 96 off just 51 balls. However, India's bowlers kept the pressure on, with Washington Sundar, Axar Patel and Shivam Dube claiming two wickets each.

Earlier, India posted a commanding 211/6 in 20 overs in the men's cricket final of the 2026 Asian Games in Nisshin on Saturday. Opener Abhishek Sharma provided a blazing start with 61 off 28 balls, while Tilak Varma remained unbeaten on 51 off 22 balls and Shivam Dube contributed a quick 27 off 14 balls, powering India past the 200-run mark.

data.title: Bitcoin Investors Who Bought Last Year's Rally Are Selling As Price Nears Their Break-Even, Glassnode Says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Glassnode said on Saturday that Bitcoin investors who bought last year's rally were selling more coins per day than at any other point this year.
  • Buyers from one to two years ago have an average cost basis near $97,000, and those from six to 12 months ago near $89,000, leaving both groups holding at a loss.
  • Holders who bought during the decline are not selling, which concentrates the supply in one group rather than across the holder base.

As Bitcoin struggled to break past $85,000 on Saturday, investors who bought into the apex cryptocurrency during last year's rally were selling more coins per day than at any other point this year, according to on-chain analytics firm Glassnode.

On X, Glassnode grouped holders by when they bought and calculated each group's average cost. That figure, known as a cost basis, marked the price at which a set of buyers breaks even. Two of those groups were below that line.

The firm said buyers from one to two years ago held an average cost basis of about $97,000, and buyers from six to 12 months ago held one of about $89,000. Both cohorts were underwater, according to Glassnode.

Bitcoin's price was around $84,673 at the time of writing. At that price, the six-to-12-month group needs a gain of roughly 5% to reach break-even, and the one-to-two-year group needs nearly 15%.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC moved to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ levels over the past day.

2025 Bitcoin Buyers Drive Selling Pressure As Other Holders Stay Put

Both groups were holding at a loss. Bitcoin was worth less now than they paid for it, so selling today meant taking that loss. Holders in that position often wait for the price to climb back to what they paid, and then sell. That way they get out without losing money. Each cost basis becomes a level where selling tends to pick up.

Glassnode's chart marked two points where Bitcoin approached those lines and turned lower. The firm labeled both "Rejected" on the chart but did not expand on them in the post. The chart measured selling as the volume of Bitcoin moved from one entity to another each day, on a seven-day average. Glassnode said the 2025-rally buyers were now moving the most coins per day of any point this year.

However, not every cohort was selling. Glassnode said holders who bought during the decline were not moving their coins. That difference narrowed where the supply was coming from. On the firm's reading, the selling was concentrated in one group of buyers rather than spread across the holder base.

A Weekly Close Is The Test

Analyst Ted Pillows set out the near-term level. He said “Bitcoin tapped the $87,000 zone” and then reversed its entire gain. Pillows said a strong rally required a weekly close above $87,500.

A weekly close was the final price of the trading week rather than an intraday high. If that close did not happen, Pillows said there was a decent chance of a correction below $80,000. That level sat below both cost-basis figures Glassnode cited.

A Firmer Relative Picture

Previously, Glassnode explained that Bitcoin's relative strength was back, with its win rate against the S&P 500 (SPX) moving above 50% last week. The win rate measured the share of trading days on which Bitcoin outperformed the index.

Glassnode said Bitcoin beat the index on only a fifth of trading days in June, which was the weakest stretch in six years. The firm said the recovery came with stocks flat, which pointed to a bid for Bitcoin itself.

Analyst Willy Woo made a longer-dated case, saying that Bitcoin had never been beaten by stocks over a four-year investment period, even for a buyer who entered at a top. He put Bitcoin's four-year compound annual growth rate at 42% against 19% for the S&P 500.

data.title: Sessions Court Orders Fresh Hearing On FIR Plea In EbixCash Greater Noida Farmhouse Dispute
data.description:
The Gautam Buddh Nagar court clarified that it had not directed the registration of an FIR and had instead remitted the matter for reconsideration through a reasoned order.

The Gautam Buddh Nagar Sessions Court has set aside an order that treated an application seeking police investigation into an alleged unlawful takeover of a farmhouse as a private complaint, holding that the magistrate had not adequately addressed the material placed before it.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Ashish Kumar Chaurasia allowed the criminal revision filed by Jyoti Kachroo and Robin Raina against the Chief Judicial Magistrate’s order dated 19 May 2025.

The revisionists had moved an application under Section 173(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, seeking the registration of an FIR and police investigation into alleged incidents at a farmhouse situated in Agricultural Greens, Greater Noida, during the intervening night of 28 and 29 September 2024.

They alleged unlawful entry, theft, damage to property and forcible possession of the premises. According to the revision petition, movable assets, vehicles and other valuable articles were removed, while a Harley-Davidson motorcycle belonging to Kachroo was subsequently recovered from the possession of one of the respondents.

The revisionists contended that their possession of the property was supported by video material, media reports and a report dated 6 October 2024 prepared by a local commissioner. They argued that the magistrate had rejected the request for police investigation without examining the allegations and supporting material in their entirety.

Respondents Cite Commercial And Arbitration Disputes

The respondents opposed the revision, questioning its maintainability and alleging concealment of material facts. They submitted that the controversy arose from a commercial transaction and was being given a criminal colour. They also referred to proceedings under Sections 9 and 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The order records that, following a complaint made by Eraaya Lifespaces Limited, the Economic Offences Wing conducted an inquiry and FIR No. 83 of 2025 was registered on 26 June 2025.

The underlying dispute concerns a proposed transaction involving property owned by Firefield Buildcon Private Limited. According to the revisionists, EbixCash Limited had agreed in November 2022 to sell the premises for ₹27 crore, of which ₹20.15 crore had allegedly been transferred. Kachroo claimed ownership and control of Firefield Buildcon and also served as one of its directors.

Magistrate’s Order Lacked Adequate Reasoning

The Sessions Court observed that its revisional jurisdiction was limited and could not be exercised as though it were hearing an appeal or reassessing the entire evidence. Intervention was nevertheless permissible where the subordinate court’s order disclosed a legal or procedural irregularity.

Referring to the Allahabad High Court’s decision in Sukhwasi v. State of Uttar Pradesh, the court noted that an application seeking police investigation need not result automatically in the registration of an FIR. A magistrate may treat such an application as a complaint, depending on the circumstances.

However, the Sessions Court found that the magistrate’s order did not specifically discuss all the facts presented by the applicants or explain why the matter should proceed only as a private complaint. This omission, it held, amounted to a legal error warranting reconsideration.

The court consequently set aside the order dated 19 May 2025 and directed the magistrate to rehear the parties and pass a fresh, reasoned order in accordance with law. The parties have been directed to appear before the magistrate on 30 October 2026.

The Sessions Court did not express any opinion on the merits of the allegations and did not direct the police to register an FIR.

data.title: Aurobindo Pharma gets USFDA final approval for Perampanel tablets
data.description:
Aurobindo Pharma Limited said on Saturday that it has received final approval from the US Food & Drug Administration (USFDA) to manufacture and market Perampanel tablets in strengths of 2 mg, 4 mg, 6 mg, 8 mg, 10 mg and 12 mg.

The approved tablets are bioequivalent and therapeutically equivalent to the reference listed drug Fycompa tablets of Catalyst Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

The product will be manufactured at Unit-IV of APL Healthcare, a wholly owned subsidiary of Aurobindo Pharma, and will be launched in Q3 FY27.

The approved product has an estimated US market size of $67 million for the 12 months ended August 2026, according to IQVIA MAT.

With this approval, Aurobindo Pharma now has a total of 599 ANDA approvals from the USFDA, comprising 574 final approvals and 25 tentative approvals.

Perampanel tablets are indicated for the treatment of partial-onset seizures, with or without secondarily generalized seizures, in patients with epilepsy aged 4 years and older.

They are also indicated as adjunctive therapy for the treatment of primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in patients with epilepsy aged 12 years and older.

Earlier on October 1, in a separate development, Aurobindo Pharma launched Adquey, its first novel drug in the US market.

Adquey, originally discovered by Otsuka Pharmaceutical and licensed to Aurobindo's arm Acrotech for US commercialisation, is a non-steroidal topical phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor used to treat mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis in adults and children aged two years and above.

The drug has patent protection until 2036. The US market for the product category was estimated at around $1.3 billion for the 12 months ended July 2026, according to IQVIA MAT.

The launch also marks Acrotech's entry into the US dermatology market. The company has established a dedicated dermatology business unit with commercial capabilities across marketing, sales and field engagement to support Adquey and build its presence in the segment.

Aurobindo Pharma shares closed 0.34% lower at ₹1,666.30 on October 1 at NSE.

data.title: Apple to replace iPhone 18 Pro Max facing AT&T glitch
data.description:
Apple has offered to replace some of the iPhone 18 Pro Max devices after “a small number” of its customers on the AT&T network faced a cellular connectivity issue.

The bug came two weeks after the $1,299 iPhone reached the market, making it the Cupertino-based tech giant’s most expensive handset, excluding its upcoming foldable phone, the iPhone Duo.

“We have identified an issue affecting a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on the AT&T network that may cause a device to lose service and be unable to make calls,” Apple told 9to5Mac.

The company has released a new version of its iOS operating system, iOS 27.0.1, and a carrier setting update for iPhone 18 Pro Max users to prevent the bug from impacting additional devices. “These updates together are meant to help prevent this issue from occurring,” the company added.

For devices already affected, the software updates will not restore cellular connectivity, and users will need a hardware replacement, Apple said. Those customers can contact Apple Support or AT&T or visit an Apple Store or AT&T location regarding the next steps.

data.title: US to lend $4.2 billion to Vistra to boost nuclear power output, source says
data.description:
The US will lend Vistra Corp about $4.2 billion to boost its nuclear power generation, a person familiar with the matter said on Saturday.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright will make the announcement on Monday at Vistra's nuclear plant along Lake Erie in Ohio, said the person, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

The loan would be used to boost power output, or "uprate" at least three of Vistra's four nuclear stations, which can be done without requiring new licenses from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

The Department of Energy and Vistra did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

According to the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, utilities can uprate nuclear plants by refueling with slightly more enriched uranium, or a higher percentage of new fuel, or through major plant modifications such as the replacement of main turbines. Utilities since the 1970s have used uprates to generate more power from reactors, the NRC's website says. As of 2022 the agency had approved more than 170 uprates, according to the NRC.

Vistra has six reactors at four US plants that generate more than 6.5 gigawatts of electricity, enough to power about 3.25 million homes.

US power demand is growing for the first time in decades, driven by surging demand from the expansion of AI data centers, electrification of transportation and cryptocurrency mining.

President Donald Trump set a goal to quadruple US nuclear power capacity by 2050. The US Department of Energy has hundreds of billions of dollars in financing available from its loan office and Wright has said the bulk of that loan capacity will support nuclear power plants.

The Vistra news was first reported by Bloomberg.

data.title: Novo Nordisk Plans Denecimib U.S. Launch In H1 2027 Amid FDA Review Extension
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Novo Nordisk A/S (NVO), a pharmaceutical company, announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) informed the company that its Biologics License Application (BLA) review of denecimig for haemophilia A treatment remains ongoing, with no new regulatory timeline communicated.

The FDA cited ongoing facility remediation activities are the cause for the extended review period. However, the agency has not identified any deficiencies related to the clinical efficacy or safety data submitted with the denecimig BLA.

Novo Nordisk submitted the denecimig BLA in September 2025 with an anticipated regulatory decision in the third quarter of 2026. Following the submission, the FDA conducted a pre-license inspection of the manufacturing site and provided feedback.

Novo Nordisk is actively implementing facility remediation activities in response to FDA feedback and working closely with the agency on outstanding requirements. The manufacturing site feedback does not impact other marketed Novo Nordisk products.

The company specified that the extended FDA review time does not affect its financial outlook for 2026. Pending regulatory decision, Novo Nordisk aims to launch denecimig in the U.S. in the first half of 2027.

Denecimig is a FVIIIa mimetic bispecific antibody designed to deliver once-monthly, every-two-weeks, and weekly prophylaxis for people living with haemophilia A, with or without inhibitors.

data.title: Nestle's low-fat dairy whitener sample found 'unsafe' in India, says regulator
data.description:
A sample of Nestle's low-fat dairy whitener collected from the Lalit hotel in New Delhi has been declared "unsafe" and "substandard," the country's food safety regulator said on Saturday.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India said in a post on X that laboratory analysis found the sample non-compliant, with authorities directing the hotel to immediately stop selling the product.

The food regulator did not make the full report public.

Nestle India said the product is safe to consume and complied with applicable regulations, adding the FSSAI report had compared total phosphorus with the limit for added phosphorus without accounting for phosphorus naturally present in milk-based ingredients.

The company spokesperson said it was engaging with authorities and had shared data on the same and similar milk-based products to show the presence of naturally occurring phosphorus.

The FSSAI did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment on Nestle's statement.

The Lalit hotel did not respond to a request for comment.

In September, the regulator said it had found a Nestle baby food sample to be substandard and was pursuing legal action against the Swiss food giant in one of its biggest growth markets.

Nestle then said its products were "fully compliant with all the applicable regulations."

data.title: Bajaj Finance shares: Jefferies India's top stock pick - 35% upside seen despite negative YTD return | Target price
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- Jefferies India's top stock recommendation: Bajaj Finance shares are one of the beaten-down stocks in the Indian stock market.

Bajaj Finance share price has fallen around 10% in one month. In YTD, Bajaj Finance shares have delivered a negative return, correcting around 2.50%. However, it figures in Jefferies India's top stock pick. The Jefferies India report dated 2 October 2026 has predicted a trend reversal in the stock, setting a Bajaj Finance share price target 35% above the current market price.

Jefferies India report dated 2 October 2026 says the Bajaj Finance board has approved a Rs.175bn ( Rs.17,500 crore) capital raise ( Rs.58bn ( Rs.5,800 crore) preferential warrants to BFS & Rs.117bn ( Rs.11,700 crore) QIP).

Tad above our expected level; 3% of mkt cap & 13% of FY27E net worth. While leverage is fair at 4.9x with a retained ROE of 17%, strong loan growth (23%), staggered monetisation of the 87% stake in BHFL, & mgt succession in Mar-28 may have led to the raise. This can lift FY28e BVPS by 8%, EPS is flat & ROE tapers marginally. BAF stays among our top picks.

Decoding the structure of the fundraise, the Jefferies India report said, "The raising involves Rs.117bn ( Rs.11,700 crore) in QIP and Rs.58bn ( Rs.5,800 crore) of warrants being assigned to Bajaj Finserv (BAF's promoter with 51% stake). It will need to invest 25% of Rs.58bn ( Rs.5,800 crore) at the time of warrant allocation, with the balance within 18 months.

Bajaj Finserv has Rs.45-50bn ( Rs.4,500 crore to Rs.5,000 crore) in cash and liquid investments, ~40% of standalone net worth, and may be able to use dividends from subsidiaries (including BALIC and BAGIC, which operate with a high Solvency Ratio of 285% and 254% respectively vs. norm of 150%) to mobilise funds towards balance investments."

Bajaj Finance share price today is Rs.947.50 apiece on the NSE, and Jefferies India report has predicted Bajaj Finance share price target of Rs.1,280, up 35% from the current market price.

Sharing the rationale behind such a whopping upside in Bajaj Finance share price, Jefferies India report said, "Our PT (Price Target) of Rs.1,280 is based on SoTP valuation. Standalone entity is valued at 5x Sep-28E P/BV. Key risks to our valuation include a slowdown in growth, higher-than-expected NIM compression, and deterioration in asset quality. Upside risks include stronger-than-expected growth in consumer durable and rural financing business, and further improvement in operating efficiencies and reduction in cost ratios."

Bajaj Finance is gearing up for one of its biggest capital-raising exercises, with the company's board approving a QIP of up to Rs.11,700 crore alongside a Rs.5,800 crore preferential issue of warrants to promoter and holding company Bajaj Finserv. The move comes as the NBFC looks to strengthen its capital base, with the proposed transactions together amounting to as much as Rs.17,500 crore.

The announcements came after the boards of both companies met on October 1, with the proposed fundraise subject to applicable regulatory and statutory approvals, including shareholder approval. Bajaj Finance said it would seek shareholder approval for both the QIP and preferential issue through an Extra Ordinary General Meeting.

The issue price for the warrants will be determined at a later stage in accordance with applicable law. Bajaj Finance said the price would be determined by its board or a duly constituted committee and would not be below the applicable floor price under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, subject to required pricing adjustments.

data.title: US Coast Guard searching for missing jet carrying 6 people bound for Boston
data.description:
By Sheila Dang

A private jet has gone missing while traveling to Boston from Bermuda with six people on board, the US Coast Guard said on Saturday.

The Federal Aviation Administration notified the Coast Guard early Saturday that it had lost contact with the plane, a Gulfstream jet used as a medical transfer aircraft, a Coast Guard spokesperson said by email.

The Coast Guard said it has dispatched air and surface crews to search for the plane near Nantucket, an affluent island community south of mainland Massachusetts.

Weather conditions in Nantucket were clear as of Saturday morning according to Accuweather.

data.title: Communication services sector rises in Q3; Meta Platforms leads gains
data.description:
The communication services gained nearly 4% in the third quarter, helped by resilience in mega-cap stocks and AI monetization, even though the broader market saw some volatility.

Communication Services Sector Q3 Scorecard

  • Sector Return: 3.58%
  • Best Performer: Meta Platforms (+24.65%)
  • Worst Performer: AppLovin (-46.31%)
  • Top Theme: Artificial Intelligence

Seeking Alpha analyst Dividend Collection Agency, Contributing analyst to the iREIT+Hoya Capital investment group, believes that the Communications sector was up primarily due to the sell-off the previous quarter.

“A lot of this had to do with interest rate and inflation uncertainty. But now that we know the Fed’s decision, this has likely curbed investor pessimism,” the analyst added.

Top communication services performers of the quarter

On the individual front, Meta Platforms was the biggest winner even though the company reported mixed second-quarter results, beating on the bottom line but missing profit expectations amid higher operational expenses. The company also expects to spend more on AI, raising the lower end of its capex guidance.

Meta Platforms revealed a new "pillar" of its business, the Meta Enterprise Platform, through which it will offer its full technology stack, including the Muse agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code, and more to help businesses and developers.

Meta was followed by AT&T and Warner Bros. Discovery .

“I believe META Platforms’ performance was due to shares being previously oversold on worries about aggressive spending during high inflation, and how hyperscalers will monetize AI going forward. AT&T’s performance was contributed to a poor price performance in the months prior to, which I think is due to higher inflation worries. Because telecoms are CAPEX intensive, higher rates could impact growth by increasing costs and churn. But the company’s recent deal with Corning to expand its fiber network and compete with Verizon , who also announced a deal with GLW likely helped boost the share price,” the analyst said.

Here are the top five gainers of the quarter:

  • Meta Platforms  +24.65%
  • AT&T +18.73%
  • Warner Bros. Discovery +16.84%
  • Fox +8.74%
  • Verizon +7.87%

Top communication services losers of the quarter:

On the other hand, AppLovin was the biggest detractor in the quarter, slipping over 46% as investors reacted to a rare revenue miss for the mobile advertising and app technology company in its second quarter financial results.

data.title: Teens Who Can't Put Down TikTok and Instagram Are Losing Their Sense of Time — WSJ
data.description:
By Julie Jargon

The constant flux of TikTok clips, Instagram reels and YouTube shorts running through our social-media feeds isn't only zapping our attention spans, it's altering how we perceive time.

"Future time perspective" is our capacity to tie our present activities to later outcomes. For students, this means seeing the benefit of studying because they know it can result in good grades, which can lead to college admission and eventually, a job. That multidimensional way of thinking allows them to set aside immediate rewards-such as watching videos or playing videogames-in favor of doing homework.

Researchers at several universities in China, in a study involving more than 1,500 high-school students, found that their future time perspective was damaged by a steady diet of such short-form videos.

These videos, in particular, activate the reward circuitry of the brain with their novel, engaging and effortless nature, leading to instant and constant gratification. We already saw in a previous study that this type of engagement activates the addiction centers of our brains, and in some cases makes it hard for us to stop viewing.

Now, it's also making us less able to plan for the future, or even care about it.

The brain effects hold true for adults, but are more pronounced in teens, says Dr. Vera Feuer, chief clinical officer at the Child Mind Institute, a mental-health treatment provider.

Adolescents already have a harder time than adults with planning ahead and controlling their impulses, because of the brain's immature prefrontal cortex. Consensus is that this part of the brain doesn't fully develop until around age 25.

"We know young people have difficulty with patience, tolerating frustration and delaying gratification. They have a harder time managing and overcoming difficulty," says Feuer, who wasn't involved in the China research.

But the study's results weren't all doom and gloom. "One new finding from this study is that the ability to overcome academic difficulty improves when there's a strong future point of view," Feuer says.

The study examined what the authors described as "academic buoyancy," or how students respond to and recover from common academic pressures and setbacks in daily learning. Students who are less equipped to handle academic setbacks, such as poor grades, are more inclined to use short-form videos as an escape, thus creating a negative cycle.

In other words, the videos may be less of a cause of this procrastination, and more a symptom of it. And helping kids set ambitious goals is one way to tie their academic work to the future and deprioritize the immediate rewards of video-watching.

"Cultivating adolescents' future time perspective is therefore crucial to counteract short-form video addiction's detrimental effects and bolster their academic buoyancy," the study's authors wrote. (They didn't respond to requests for comment.)

What parents can do

Social-media companies, under fire from regulators and lawsuits, have been making changes to curb youth addiction to their products, including providing break reminders in the apps, turning off push notifications at night and disabling video autoplay for teen accounts.

As part of Meta Platforms's recent $18 billion settlement with 48 states to keep children safer online, the tech giant agreed to put in place a two-hour daily limit for teens across Instagram and Facebook as well as to block the apps's main feeds between the hours of midnight and 6 a.m. Meta is calling on TikTok, YouTube and Snap to agree to place the same daily time limits and nighttime restrictions on their apps.

Here are some ways parents can help their children stay on task:

Set your own app limits. As burdensome as parental controls can be, the easiest way to do it is to set device-level app time limits. This can be done by setting up Family Sharing on Apple devices, Google Family Link on Android devices or doing it directly from the screen-time settings of the actual phone. With supervised accounts, parents can set a time limit on YouTube Shorts-or turn off the short videos altogether.

Discuss when short videos are OK. If the kids really want to watch these short videos, set times of day or points during the week when they're allowed, and be sure to reinforce why you're implementing these restrictions.

Silence the phone. Have your children put their phones in focus mode while they're doing their homework so they don't receive text and social-media notifications.

Get phones out of the bedroom. Kids shouldn't be on their phones while doing their homework-though they might argue they need them for calculators and other look-ups. It's even more important to keep phones out of their rooms at night, to ensure adequate sleep.

Have them practice mindfulness. "Mindfulness" can feel like a woo-woo term, but one study found that mindfulness accounted for about half the link between short-form video addiction and lower academic engagement. Doing a brief mindfulness exercise before each study session can help students focus, it said.

Write to Julie Jargon at Julie.Jargon@wsj.com

data.title: "Nagoya and Japan have written a proud new chapter in cricket's history": ICC Chairman Jay Shah congratulates Team India on Asian Games gold
data.description:
Aichi-Nagoya, Oct. 3 -- Team India celebrates a historic double at the Asian Games as the men's team clinched the Gold medal in Nagoya, following the women's team's Gold-winning campaign last week.

It is India's second straight men's cricket Gold at the Asian Games, as the Men in Blue continued their golden run in T20Is this year, following their second consecutive ICC Men's T20 World Cup title earlier this year.

ICC Chairman Jay Shah, BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) President PT Usha, among others, were in attendance as Jay Shah presented the Gold medals to Shreyas Iyer-led Team India.

"Nagoya and Japan have written a proud new chapter in cricket's history. Congratulations to Team India on a campaign worthy of this moment, and heartfelt thanks to every competing nation, to the Olympic Council of Asia and organisers whose vision brought us here, and to the thousands of fans whose presence reminded us why cricket is so special anywhere in the world," ICC Chairman Jay Shah said after Team India clinched the Asiad Gold.

Following the women's team's triumph, India's men also defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the gold medal clash at the ongoing Asian Games on Saturday, with stellar performances from Abhishek Sharma, Tilak Varma and Axar Patel powering the team to victory.

Chasing a massive target of 212, Pakistan's Hasan Nawaz stood out as a lone warrior, smashing 96 off just 51 balls. However, India's bowlers kept the pressure on, with Washington Sundar, Axar Patel and Shivam Dube claiming two wickets each.

Earlier, India posted a commanding 211/6 in 20 overs in the men's cricket final of the 2026 Asian Games in Nisshin on Saturday.

Opener Abhishek Sharma provided a blazing start with 61 off 28 balls, while Tilak Varma remained unbeaten on 51 off 22 balls and Shivam Dube contributed a quick 27 off 14 balls, powering India past the 200-run mark.

data.title: After Sept, bond yields to peak in Oct too? Experts decode future of Indian bond market; RBI's next move holds key
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- India's bond market is entering October with the comfort of strong domestic growth but the discomfort of rising inflationary pressures, elevated global yields and tighter liquidity conditions.

The sharp rise in the domestic 10-year benchmark yield in September has changed the complexion of the fixed-income market, with investors now having to navigate a combination of geopolitical uncertainty, oil prices, central-bank policy and potential additional supply.

The domestic 10-year yield rose around 30 basis points in September to approximately 7.20%, following an 11-basis-point increase in August. It was 6.6% at the start of the year. The move tracked the global bond market, with the US 10-year Treasury yield rising around 53 basis points to 5.22%.

Milan Mody, Executive Vice President and Fund Manager, Fixed Income at 360 ONE Asset, said the September environment was shaped by persistent US-Iran tensions, higher crude prices and tighter global monetary policy.

"Tensions between the US and Iran continued to simmer through September, keeping oil prices firmly above US$100 per barrel. As inflationary risks intensified, global central banks tightened policy, with the US Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan each raising policy rates," Mody said.

Indian bond yields are likely to remain under pressure as the Reserve Bank of India works to absorb surplus liquidity while market participants track borrowing needs, inflation and global bond yields.

Mody expects the Indian debt market to remain under pressure, with the yield curve potentially shifting gradually higher in parallel. The monsoon season ended with a deficit of around 15%, while elevated oil prices and global bond yields could add to pressure on domestic yields.

"The direction of policy rates appears increasingly clear, with market participants gradually converging on a higher-for-longer interest rate outlook. In our view, the Indian debt market is likely to move sideways under pressure, with a gradual, parallel upward shift," Mody said.

At the same time, he believes yields are moving towards a more reasonable valuation zone. The market, however, is already factoring in a 75-basis-point rate hike and a gradual increase in inflation.

The eventual inclusion of fully accessible route securities in the Bloomberg index could provide support to Indian bonds.

Foreign portfolio investors have remained a source of support, with net purchases during the year so far standing at US$5.5 billion.

The direction of yields in October could depend heavily on developments in the US-Iran conflict and movements in bond yields in Japan and the US.

Domestically, the RBI's communication on inflation and its approach towards surplus liquidity at the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting could become important triggers.

For the medium to long term, Mody expects the 10-year benchmark to remain within a defined range, although geopolitical risks could keep yields elevated in the near term.

"In our view, the absence of a resolution to the West Asia conflict is likely to keep domestic yields elevated in the near term, and we expect the 10-year benchmark to trade between 7.05% and 7.20%," Mody said.

For fixed-income portfolios, 360 ONE Asset remains neutral on duration and prefers greater exposure to short- to medium-maturity corporate bonds. Mody said the risk from higher yields appeared more pronounced in ultra-long maturities, while credit quality remained strong.

Shorter-tenure corporate bonds, therefore, could offer a better risk-reward trade-off in the current environment, while dynamic bond funds may suit investors seeking flexibility across credit and duration, depending on their risk profile and investment horizon.

Mody believes the RBI's monetary policy is at an inflection point, with higher food prices linked to El Niño conditions and rising oil prices adding upside risks to inflation. Against this backdrop, liquidity management could become increasingly important for the central bank.

He expects the repo rate to rise by 50 to 75 basis points by next year, describing the move as a recalibration aimed at bringing rates closer to neutral levels while supporting the currency. Forex management is expected to remain another key area for investors to monitor.

He also expects the RBI to rely on a combination of OMO sales and sell-buy swaps to manage surplus liquidity. His estimates point towards OMO sales of around Rs.2 trillion and US$35 billion, equivalent to approximately Rs.3.3 trillion, through FX maturity or sell-buy swaps.

data.title: Meta’s Justin Osofsky joins Nscale as COO ahead of IPO: Bloomberg
data.description:
Nscale has hired Justin Osofksy, a long-term executive at Meta Platforms , to be its chief operating officer to drive a rapid expansion at the AI infrastructure company tied to its upcoming IPO, Bloomberg News reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

Osofksy, who served Meta for 18 years in various capacities and was most recently its chief partnerships officer, will report to Nscale CEO Josh Payne and lead the company’s global operations, the person said.

A slate of Meta veterans, including former Chief Operating Officer Sheryl Sandberg, already serve Nscale , a neo-cloud operator that rents out computing power to AI developers.

Sandberg, who sits on the company's board, helped hire Nick Clegg, the Facebook operator’s former head of global affairs, and Fidji Simo, a former OpenAI executive.

In September, the London-based data center operator filed for a U.S. IPO, an offering expected to raise as much as $3B, Bloomberg previously reported.

Meta announced the resignation in an internal post, with Chief Operating Officer Javier Olivan noting that Osofksy had “brought sound judgment and steady leadership that will outlast his time here.”

data.title: SoftBank-backed Starfish gets ₹88.3 crore from AceVector IPO exit
data.description:
SoftBank-backed Starfish I Pte Ltd emerged as the biggest beneficiary among selling shareholders in Snapdeal parent AceVector’s ₹420 crore initial public offering (IPO), securing about ₹88.3 crore through the offer-for-sale (OFS) component.

Starfish, AceVector’s largest shareholder, sold 2.76 crore shares at the IPO’s upper price of ₹32 apiece, accounting for roughly two-thirds of the total OFS proceeds. According to AceVector’s red herring prospectus (RHP), the shares sold represented a 0.08X return multiple.

Starfish will continue to hold 11.3 crore shares in AceVector following the IPO, worth about ₹361.8 crore at the issue price.

AceVector, the parent of e-commerce marketplace Snapdeal and e-commerce enablement platform Unicommerce, raised ₹287 crore through a fresh issue, while existing shareholders offered up to 4.16 crore shares through the OFS. At ₹32 a share, the issue valued the company at about ₹1,741 crore.

The IPO, which closed on September 29, was subscribed 4.93 times, with the company set to list on the BSE and NSE on October 5.

Nexus sees divergent returns

Nexus Venture Partners also secured a partial exit through multiple investment vehicles, though the returns varied significantly across funds.

Nexus India Direct Investments II sold 73.9 lakh shares for ₹23.6 crore, representing a 1.03X return multiple. The fund will retain 3 crore shares, worth about ₹96.7 crore at the IPO price.

Nexus Opportunity Fund Ltd sold 8.4 lakh shares for ₹2.6 crore at a 0.14X return multiple, while Nexus Ventures III sold 4.6 lakh shares for ₹1.4 crore, translating into a 0.07X multiple.

Other shareholders sell shares

Other selling shareholders included FIH Business Global, Rupen Investment and Industries and Centaurus Trading and Investments. FIH sold 17.4 lakh shares for ₹5.6 crore, while Rupen Investment and Centaurus each sold 2.7 lakh shares for about ₹86 lakh.

AceVector to deploy fresh capital

AceVector intends to use the fresh capital primarily for marketing and business promotion of its marketplace business, technology infrastructure, acquisitions, and general corporate purposes. The company reported a consolidated loss of ₹60.7 crore in FY26, while revenue from operations rose 29.2% to ₹510.4 crore.

data.title: Nestle's low-fat dairy whitener sample found 'unsafe', 'substandard' in India
data.description:
A sample of Nestle's low-fat dairy whitener collected from the Lalit hotel in New Delhi has been declared "unsafe" and "substandard," the country's food safety regulator said on Saturday.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India said in a post on X that laboratory analysis found the sample non-compliant, with authorities directing the hotel to immediately stop selling the product.

The food regulator did not make the full report public.

The Lalit and Nestle did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

In September, the regulator said it had found a Nestle baby food sample to be substandard and was pursuing legal action against the Swiss food giant in one of its biggest growth markets.

Nestle then said its products were "fully compliant with all the applicable regulations."

data.title: What defines the new lot of running shoes for peak performance
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- Buoyed by the podium finishes for India's long and middle distance runners-including three medals for Gulveer Singh and a silver medal for marathoner Sawan Barwal, at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya in Japan this year-recreational runners are enthusiastically welcoming the running season in India.

How to hit a new personal best is on the minds of tens of thousands as races start coming thick and fast, including World Majors such as Chicago Marathon and New York City Marathon and the homegrown Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon on October 18. Beyond proper training, the answer lies in choosing shoes that can help you reach your goals, believes Romain Girard, Global Head of Innovation for footwear at PUMA Group, as he looks at several shoe prototypes sitting in a black box in front of him at the company's headquarters in Herzogenaurauch, Germany.

Every major sports brand seems to believe so. Nike's newest race day shoes-including Nike Apex, Alpha Fly 4 and Swoosh Fly-are for runners of varying abilities ranging from elite athletes to slow or medium-paced recreational athletes.

Adidas recently launched Adizero Adios Pro 5 aimed at fast recreational runners and has just announced a new shoe for slower ones where they can switch on and switch off the carbon plate mid-run depending on how they are feeling. The carbon-plate is lodged between a thick layer of lightweight midsole foam used in performance footwear.

PUMA has Velocity without any carbon plates. But, it's present in the Deviate range for seasoned runners and the Fast-R race day shoes for the elite. The reason, argues Girard, for launching high performance shoes for runners of very different capabilities is because everyone loves the feeling of running faster, no matter what end of the speed spectrum they maybe at. "Running shoes have to be relevant not only to the elite but to mass athletes too," he adds. And to make that happen sports brands will need to innovate-be it with shapes, silhouettes, new technologies or materials.

Based on the level of an athlete's performance ranging from two-hour marathoners to six-hour marathoners, brands are designing shoes with the appropriate level of technology and architecture to ensure cushioning and speed. Now that every single running shoe brand uses carbon fibre plates in their shoes, the advancements are happening elsewhere.

Nike has been experimenting with full-length Nike Air units underfoot, Adidas has experimented with a carbon rim that can be switched on and off, while PUMA has focussed on the foam and out-of-the-box architecture to help people achieve their goals of getting faster.

Among the prototypes I was privy to, a couple of shoes had double carbon plates (including one designed specifically for Hyrox), at least two pairs had extreme cushioning rendering them illegal for World Athletics competitions as rules mandate a maximum cushioning of 40mm, and another that is set to be launched shortly, had two carbon plates. "A runner's journey has changed over the years.

Athletes who run on the weekends and enjoy speed do not need to stick to legal shoes. There are multiple shades of racing today from community runs to party runs and park runs. These athletes can use the extra cushioning and other design innovations to enjoy the feeling of running faster," points out Girard while I tried out the pair that resembled high heels minus the heels.

All leading sports brands have decoupled technology and architecture as per the modern athlete's needs. Girard and his team developed their trademarked Nitro foam during the Covid pandemic. According to him, Covid was when running really exploded into the massive mass participation sport that it has become today.

Races sell out within hours of opening registrations. Indian running groups this week pointed out the Ahmedabad Marathon was sold out within hours of its announcement. The Tata Mumbai Marathon registrations were full despite several runners complaining about the high registration fees across their categories with Rs.5000 for the full marathon.

Next year's London Marathon is set to make history with 100,000 runners over a two-day event. "Running is a huge world already and it is going to get bigger," says Girard, and adds, "And, innovation has two gears - evolution and revolution." The evolution of the foam and shoe architecture are happening as we speak. Revolution will come as the running world expands.

data.title: Manipur: Nutritional food baskets distributed to patients under TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan
data.description:
Imphal, Oct. 3 -- A distribution ceremony for nutritional food baskets to TB patients and family caregivers in Manipur was held on Saturday at the Manipur State Film Development Society (MSFDS), Imphal, under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan of the National TB Elimination Programme.

The program was organised by the National Health Mission and Directorate of Health Services, Government of Manipur, with nutritional support provided through the Nikshay Mitra initiative by the National Thermal Power Corporation Limited (NTPC) under its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program.

The ceremony was attended by Governor of Manipur Ajay Kumar Bhalla, Chief Secretary of Manipur Rajeev Singh Thakur, NTPC Chairman and Managing Director Gurdeep Singh, and Commissioner of Health and Family Welfare Sumant Singh.

As part of the program, nutritional food baskets were distributed across all 15 districts of Manipur to support TB patients and their family caregivers. Handheld X-ray machines were also distributed to strengthen TB screening and detection services across the state.

Addressing the gathering, Governor Ajay Kumar Bhalla emphasised the need to collectively fight tuberculosis, stressing that TB is a curable disease and encouraging patients to remain strong and complete their treatment. He also appreciated the efforts of the organisations and individuals who contributed to making the program successful.

State TB Officer Dr. Hemalata Thokchom delivered a vote of thanks, acknowledging the support and cooperation extended by the stakeholders involved in the initiative.

Thokchom told ANI, "Nutritional support is a must in order to improve their immunity status. Everybody voluntarily - it may be an organisation, an individual, or a corporate - can register themselves to support the TB patients by giving this food basket, which contains all the essential elements like rice, pulses, and nutrient-dense food items."

Commissioner (Health and Family Welfare), Government of Manipur, Sumant Singh, IAS, delivered the keynote address, highlighting the importance of nutritional support, early detection and collective efforts in achieving the goal of a TB-free Manipur.

The initiative aims to provide nutritional assistance to TB patients while strengthening the state's efforts towards the National TB Elimination Programme and the broader goal of eliminating tuberculosis from India.

data.title: US-Iran war impact: Nayara Energy hikes fuel prices in India with immediate effect; petrol up by Rs.5, diesel by Rs.3
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- Pressure continues to mount on fuel retailers amid higher global energy prices, as Nayara Energy, India's largest private fuel retailer, has increased fuel prices with immediate effect. Petrol prices have been increased by Rs.5 per litre, while diesel prices have risen by Rs.3 per litre.

The latest hike marks another price revision by Nayara Energy this year, as Indian refiners deal with the impact of geopolitical disruptions on global crude oil and fuel markets, news agency PTI reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

According to the report, India's largest private fuel retailer, which operates over 7,000 fuel stations across the country, announced the price hike, with effect from early hours on Saturday.

When the US-Iran war disrupted energy supplies after breaking out in late February, Nayara Energy became the first fuel retailer to pass the impact of higher international oil prices on to consumers. On March 26, the company raised petrol and diesel prices by Rs.5 and Rs.3 per litre, respectively, taking the rates at its outlets to Rs.100.71 and Rs.91.31 per litre, respectively.

However, Nayara Energy later reversed the March price hike. On 1 July, the largest private fuel retailer slashed petrol prices by Rs.5 and diesel by Rs.3 a litre. The reduction came after global crude prices eased as tensions in West Asia subsided. It was the first reduction by a fuel retailer in over two years and subsequently brought Nayara's pricing back in line with state-owned retailers.

The latest increase signals another effort by the private fuel retailer to reflect rising costs in retail prices following a period of relatively stable rates.

In contrast, state-owned fuel retailers began transferring the impact of higher international oil prices to consumers in May. They raised petrol and diesel prices through a series of staggered increases, with the cumulative hike reaching around Rs.7.50 per litre for both fuels by the end of May. The fourth increase, announced on 25 May, was Rs.2.61 per litre for petrol and Rs.2.71 per litre for diesel.

State-owned oil marketing companies (OMCs), including Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, have a market share of over 90 per cent of India's 1,04,137 petrol pumps, and have historically kept prices relatively stable, despite fluctuations in global crude prices.
